4. The suit was contested by the Government by filing written statement denying the material averments made in the plaint and stating, inter alia, that the land in suit is a fishery and as such on the acquisition of rent receiving interest vested in the Government and thereupon the Government is possessing the land in suit treating the same as fisheries and is leasing out the fisheries to different persons, that fringes of the fisheries are leased out for boro cultivation, that the plaintiffs' deeds are fraudulent and ante-dated, that Loke Patni and others had no saleable interest in the land in suit. 

 5. The trial Court on consideration of the materials on record held that Ext.5 khatian shows that Loke Patni and others possessed the land in suit for use on behalf of their co-villagers and the same is Jalkar, that Ext.2 patta and Ext.5 khatian shows that only Jalkar was leased out and Exts.6 and 6(a) show that the land in suit is marshy land and thus from the said documents it is seen that the land in suit is beel land and in all probability in the fringe of the Jalkar fishery boro is cultivated, that the land in suit is not the boro land but Jalkar, that Loke Patni and others did not acquire any saleable interest in the land in suit and they had only jalker right in suit, as evidenced by Ext. c, record has been prepared in the name of the Government, that no material has been brought on record to show that after purchase in 1955 plaintiffs paid rent, that no explanation has been offered for not producing the original kabalas on the basis whereof plaintiffs are claiming the land in suit, that there is no averment in the plaint as to why the plaintiffs are not in possession of the kabalas by which they have purchased the land in suit, that at the time of trial attempt was made through the deposition of P.W.2 that the kabalas were stolen but as there was no such case in the pleading the said deposition can not be taken into consideration, that averments made as to cause of action are not true, that in the totality of the facts it appear that Ext.4 by which plaintiffs said to have purchased the land in suit is not genuine, that from Exts. (a) and (b) it is seen that the land in suit is fishery and the Government auctioned the same and thus it is seen that the land in suit is not boro land, that plaintiffs have not acquired any right, title and interest in the land in suit on the basis of their allege purchases since the land is fishery vested with the Government on the acquisition of rent receiving interest. On the aforesaid findings the trial Court dismissed the suit. The appellate Court upon reversing the judgment and decree of the trial Court allowed the appeal and decreed the suit on the findings that from the Government's side no paper was produced to show that the land in suit was fishery and on the acquisition of rent receiving interest the same vested in the Government and as regard the land in suit no C.A. Roll was prepared and as such interest in the land in suit remains with the tenant and consequent thereupon the plaintiffs by their purchase from the recorded tenants acquired right, title and interest in the land in suit, that S.A. record Ext.5 was prepared without any basis. 

 6. The Government moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction and obtained Rule. The High Court Division on consideration of the materials on record, particularly Memo No. SA/IMA-373/73/1219(38) dated 1.8.1973 and the Memo No. SA/IMA-52/72/215- JM dated 7.12.1973 arrived at the finding that the land in suit in fact is a fishery and known as Mohal. Shamil Fisheries, that record shows that Loke Patni and others were given settlement of the Mohal Shamil Fisheries on taking ground rent as they were representing the villagers, that plaintiffs' vendor had no title in the land in suit and they had representative character as regard the land in suit, that plaintiffs by their alleged purchase did not acquire any title in the land in suit. The High Court Division also observed that since the plaintiffs are in possession and they are representing the villagers as such their prayer for permanent injunction from leasing out the land in suit which is fishery to outsider is maintainable. In our view this observation of the High Court Division is unwarranted since the admitted position is that fishery is non-retainable after the acquisition of rent receiving interest and on the acquisition of rent receiving interest fishery vested in the Government and as such it is for the Government to deal with the fishery in question in the way it considers will secure the interest of the State or in other words the Government is quite competent to lease out the fisheries through auction or through negotiation if thereby interest of the Government is best served. 

 8. From the consideration of the materials on record as it is seen that the land in suit is fisheries and consequent thereupon on the acquisition of rent receiving interest as per the provision of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 the fishery has vested in the Government and as such plaintiffs by purchase from the Loke Patni and others who were representing villagers and who had no saleable interest in the land in suit, did not acquire any title.
